description: Excel to fixed-width text: turn a sheet of an XLSX, XLS or ODS workbook into plain text with aligned columns for emails, logs and terminals. No upload.
heading: Excel to Fixed-Width Text Converter
subtitle: Pick a sheet and get plain text with every column lined up; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Turn an Excel sheet into fixed-width plain text in your browser: each column is padded to its widest cell, columns are separated by a gap of 1 to 4 spaces, and the header is underlined with dashes. Paste it into an email, a code comment, a ticket or a terminal, or download a .txt file.

features.title: Lined up
features.text: Each column is padded to its widest cell, and wide characters count as two, so columns stay straight.

features.title: Private
features.text: The workbook is read by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert Excel to fixed-width text

steps.title: Choose your workbook
steps.text: Drop an .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm or .ods file on this page, choose it, or try a sample. It is read in your browser and never uploaded.

steps.title: Pick the sheet
steps.text: The first sheet becomes aligned text at once; choose another from the sheet list.

steps.title: Set the gap
steps.text: Choose 1 to 4 spaces between columns, and the text updates.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Copy the text, or download it as a .txt file.

handlesTitle: What the Excel to fixed-width converter handles
handles: Files: .xlsx, .xls (Excel 97–2003), .xlsm and .ods workbooks, one sheet at a time.
Layout: every column padded to its widest cell, with a gap of 1 to 4 spaces; empty rows are skipped.
Header: the first row, underlined with a line of dashes.
Wide characters: Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count as two columns, as a monospaced font draws them.
Values: each cell as Excel shows it, so formulas give their result and dates and prices keep their format.
limits: Columns line up only in a monospaced font, such as a terminal, code editor or plain-text email.
One very long cell makes its whole column that wide, and password-protected workbooks cannot be opened.
faqTitle: Excel to fixed-width text: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the workbook and writes the text on your device. Nothing is sent to a server, saved on the site or kept in a history.

faq.question: Why do the columns not line up where I pasted them?
faq.answer: Fixed-width text needs a monospaced font, where every character has the same width. In a proportional font, such as most email defaults, the columns drift.

faq.question: How wide is each column?
faq.answer: As wide as its widest cell, header included, plus the gap you choose between columns: 1 to 4 spaces.

faq.question: Do Chinese or Japanese characters break the alignment?
faq.answer: No. Wide characters are counted as two columns, as monospaced fonts draw them, so the next column still starts in the right place.

faq.question: Can I turn it back into a spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Excel can split fixed-width text with Data > Text to Columns and the Fixed width option, using the gaps between columns.

faq.question: Is a long sheet converted in full?
faq.answer: Yes. The preview shows the first 5,000 lines, but Copy and Download take the whole text.

faq.question: How do I convert an Excel sheet to fixed-width text?
faq.answer: Open the workbook, pick the sheet and the gap between columns, then copy the aligned text or download it as a .txt file. OpenAnyDoc pads each column in your browser, so the workbook is never uploaded.
